title: Proactive congestion-island detection and sticky-region guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a progressive traffic surge on 2026-03-09 we observed cross-region failover amplification that caused an SLO miss for request p99 latency and error rate for hosted inference customers. Secondary regions entered a congestion mode that persisted despite circuit-breaker trips; routing replays and probe jitter amplified load to warm caches and overloaded GPUS. This ticket captures the postmortem analysis and prescribes mitigations and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
incident_timeline:
2026-03-09 09:12 UTC - Automated health checks detected increased tail latency in region-eu-west-1.
2026-03-09 09:18 UTC - Smart routing triggered failover policy to reroute ~18% of traffic to region-us-west-2 (secondary).
2026-03-09 09:21 UTC - Circuit breakers in us-west-2 tripped and then rapidly reset due to short hysteresis config; controllers replayed queued requests.
2026-03-09 09:26 UTC - Observed progressive KV cache cold misses and repeated replays; GPU utilization saturated and request queues began to grow.
2026-03-09 09:40 UTC - On-call rotated, emergency mitigation (partial traffic pause to a warm standby) executed at 09:47 UTC.
2026-03-09 10:30 UTC - Traffic rebalanced with stricter admission control; SLOs recovered by 11:15 UTC but p99 latency remained degraded for the remainder of the day for some customers.
symptoms_and_impact:
- SLOs: p99 generation latency for hosted API exceeded SLO by ~220ms for 45 minutes; error rate increased from 0.15% to 1.9%.
- Affected customers: multiple production customers experienced elevated tail latency and intermittent 5xx errors; several support tickets opened.
- Operational pain: manual interventions required to rebalance traffic and warm caches, leading to longer mitigation time than expected.
root_causes: Aggressive failover policy without region-congestion damping: policy moved significant traffic quickly without detecting capacity headroom in target region.
Insufficient circuit-breaker hysteresis and rapid reset logic: short reset window led to oscillation and replay amplification instead of sustained shedding.
Admission control thresholds and queue high-water marks were tuned for steady-state rather than surge conditions; queues allowed long backpressure tail leading to GPU saturation.
Probes and health checks were noisy during failover and triggered repeated cache-warming requests (probe replay amplification).
Lack of a congestion-island detector that can identify localized overload and quarantine it from global routing decisions.
immediate_mitigations_taken: Executed emergency partial pause of non-critical routed traffic to us-west-2 to limit incoming load (09:47 UTC).
Manually increased circuit-breaker hysteresis to prevent rapid reset (temporary change in control plane).
Applied conservative admission control at the ingress (lower concurrency per model) to buy time for cache warmup.
Opened high-priority support thread with affected customers and provided visibility and ETA for stabilization.
action_items: ENG: Implement congestion-island detector in smart-routing that tracks per-region moving-window saturation (queue depth, GPU util, p99) and can tag regions as 'quarantined' for routing decisions — owner: Marcus Chen, due: 2026-04-08.
ENG/Infra: Add sustained-hysteresis mode to circuit-breaker controller so resets require multiple consecutive healthy probe windows (reduce oscillation) — owner: Priya Rao, due: 2026-03-31.
ENG: Introduce a probe-damping layer: rate-limit probe-triggered generation and mark probe traffic to avoid cache warmup amplification — owner: Elena Gomez, due: 2026-03-28.
ENG/Runtime: Add admission-control headroom logic that enforces a safety margin (X% reserved capacity) for failovers to avoid immediate saturation — owner: Akira Tanaka, due: 2026-04-05.
SRE: Create synthetic SLO canaries that run cross-region under controlled load to validate failover policies weekly — owner: SRE Team (rotation), due: 2026-03-25.
PM/Eng: Update failover runbook to include stepwise traffic ramp, explicit circuit-breaker hysteresis ops, and emergency pause playbook — owner: Diego Morales, due: 2026-03-22.
DX/Support: Produce customer-facing incident summary and post-incident mitigation guidance for customers with tight latency requirements — owner: Lina Park, due: 2026-03-18.
Eng: Add automatic rollback guard: if p99 latency exceeds SLO by threshold after failover, automatically revert routing for affected subset — owner: Marcus Chen, due: 2026-04-12.
Security/Compliance: Validate that any new telemetry or synthetic traffic adheres to PII policies (no customer payloads) — owner: Noah Singh, due: 2026-03-26.
follow_up_reviews_and_checks: Weekly verification of congestion detector false-positive rate on staged traffic for 4 weeks after rollout.
Post-change load test simulating 2x normal surge with gradual failover to ensure admission-control headroom works as intended.
Audit circuit-breaker configuration across all regions to align hysteresis settings and document rationale.
Runbook tabletop exercise scheduled for Cycle 12 to validate runbook steps under simulated multi-region surge.
telemetry_and_dashboards: New metrics created: region.congestion_score (composite), region.queue_depth_p99, circuit_breaker.reset_count, probe-replay-rate.
Dashboard: 'Regional Congestion Overview' with color-coded scores and drilldown to per-cluster queue and GPU saturation graphs.
Alert: create an alert when region.congestion_score > 0.7 for 3m with automatic paging to SRE on-call.
Tracing: tag replay-triggered calls with 'probe=true' to track amplification paths in traces.
postmortem_notes: Key lesson: failover needs to be conservative by default and surfaced to operators with clear safety margins. Rapid circuit-breaker resets intended to restore service can instead amplify load when caches are cold. We need a layered approach: detect congestion islands, prevent oscillation with stable hysteresis, quench probe amplification, and reserve headroom for failovers.
risks_and_open_questions: How aggressively should congestion detectors quarantine a region before operator intervention? (balancing availability vs containment)
Trade-offs between admission-control headroom and overall throughput/cost for steady-state customers.
Potential unexpected interactions with Dedicated customers with pinned capacity — ensure quarantine doesn't violate contracts.
review_feedback: PM review (Diego): add customer communication template and list of top affected tenants before changes go live.
SRE review (Lina): recommend a gradual rollout with feature flagging and canary scales to avoid cluster-wide surprises.
Security review (Noah): ensure synthetic canaries are scrubbed and that telemetry metadata does not include PII.
references: ENG-62107, ENG-14021 (related tickets referenced during postmortem)
